archetype.name: Playoff Team (offense-first)
archetype.definition: A Ravens team whose top-six offense, built on an efficient Lamar Jackson passing game and a Derrick Henry ground attack, carries a middling defense that cannot pressure the quarterback or protect against the deep ball.

report.headline: Elite offense against soft defenses; the pass rush is the real question
report.take:
Baltimore is 4-1 under first-year coach Jesse Minter, and the record matches the play better than most early-season marks do. The Ravens rank 5th in net EPA, their point differential is +5.4 a game, and they are only 0.8 wins over expectation. This is an offense team. They rank 2nd in success rate and 5th in pass EPA, and the line allows pressure on just 15% of dropbacks (4th). Minter has also leaned on the run, with a pass rate 6 points under expected (27th) and a 6th-ranked run EPA, and he has gone for it on every fourth-down chance the model flags. After 2025's 8-9 season, when the offense slid to 13th, this looks much more like the 2024 group that led the league.

The asterisk is the schedule. Four of the five defenses they have faced now rank 25th or worse in EPA, and Dallas is dead last. The 41-point opener and the passing explosions against Dallas and Tennessee came against bad units, so the 29.2 points a game is inflated somewhat. Week 5 is the most important data point for that reason. With Tyler Huntley at quarterback, at Atlanta's 7th-ranked defense as a 3.5-point underdog, they ran for 208 yards and won by seven. The passing game fell to 2.7 EPA from the 10-12 range of Jackson's good games. The floor without Jackson is real, but it runs entirely through Henry.

The defense is where the numbers mislead in both directions. A 9th-ranked success rate allowed and the 3rd-best EPA on short passes say the underneath coverage and tackling are sound. A 28th-ranked pressure rate, 25th on deep passes, and opposing WR1s posting 0.76 EPA per target (31st) say the opposite on anything vertical. Offenses are not dinking them to death; they are waiting for one shot downfield. This is not new: the defense ranked 10th in 2024, 18th in 2025 and is 19th now. Trey Hendrickson, a 63%-snap edge player, is now out after finger surgery. The pass rush, its biggest weakness, gets thinner.

Add 8.8 penalties a game (27th), line penalties ranked 29th, special teams costing about a point a game, and a 30th-ranked short-yardage conversion rate. This is a team leaving free points on the field. A healthy Jackson makes it a playoff team with upside. The division is three 3-2 teams, and a back half with six divisional games will decide it.

strengths.title: Efficient, low-pressure passing offense
strengths.body: With Jackson, the passing game ranks 5th in EPA and the offense 2nd in success rate, supported by a line that allows the 2nd-lowest QB hit rate. Some of the explosive weeks came against bottom-tier defenses, but the protection and efficiency are consistent with 2024's league-best offense. That points to a real, repeatable profile rather than a fluke.

strengths.title: Henry-led run game travels anywhere
strengths.body: The Ravens average 4.8 yards a carry (4th) with the 6th-best run EPA, and Henry has 113 of the backs' carries. The run game is quarterback-proof. It produced 208 yards and 7.3 EPA in Huntley's start against a top-10 defense, which is why the floor without Jackson holds.

strengths.title: Underneath coverage and tackling hold
strengths.body: Opponents succeed on only 41.9% of plays (9th) and get almost nothing on short throws (3rd). The lead back gets little in the passing game too, at 3rd-stingiest. The structure is sound, and it forces offenses to beat Baltimore over the top.

concerns.title: No pass rush, leaky deep coverage
concerns.body: A 15.8% pressure rate (28th) gives quarterbacks time to push the ball downfield. Deep passes and WR1s are among the league's worst matchups for this defense. Losing Hendrickson makes the rush worse, so expect this to persist until he returns.

concerns.title: Jackson's ankle and a thin middle
concerns.body: Jackson is listed out with an ankle sprain, though Minter says he is 'definitely doing better.' Center Cam Jurgens, a 100%-snap starter, is in the final stages of concussion protocol. The Huntley version won at Atlanta, but the passing game dropped off sharply and he took four sacks. The 6th-ranked offense is a Jackson number.

concerns.title: Self-inflicted drag: flags and specials
concerns.body: Line penalties are 29th and total penalties 27th, including 131 penalty yards against Tennessee. Special teams and short-yardage conversion are both bottom-12. These are fixable coaching issues for a new staff, but they are why heavy favorites like Tennessee and New Orleans stayed close or won.

trend.note: Margins of +18, -7, +3, +6 and +7 show an offense that has produced every week and a defense that keeps games closer than they should be. The best result, a road win as an underdog, came with the backup quarterback.

nextGame.headline: Henry against a Browns front missing two interior tackles
nextGame.body:
Cleveland is 3-2 on a -3.8 point differential, with the 5th-most wins over expectation. That is a team living on close-game luck. Its strength matches Baltimore's preferred weakness poorly for Cleveland. The pass defense is 4th in EPA and the sack rate is 5th, but the run defense is 29th in EPA and allows the league's highest explosive-run rate with a 29th-ranked missed-tackle rate. Offenses already run on the Browns more than usual. A run-first Ravens plan, whether Jackson or Huntley starts, attacks exactly that. On the other side, Cleveland's offense is 25th in EPA, cannot run (31st) and gives up sacks on 10.3% of dropbacks (32nd). Baltimore's pass rush is too weak to fully cash that in.

Availability tilts toward Baltimore on the ground. Cleveland defensive tackles Mason Graham and Mike Hall Jr. are both out, and linebacker Carson Schwesinger, a 100%-snap player, is questionable with an ankle sprain. That is the middle of the run defense. Baltimore's own concerns are at quarterback (Jackson's ankle), center (Jurgens nearing clearance) and edge (Hendrickson out). Cleveland's RB Quinshon Judkins and WR KC Concepcion are questionable, and Deshaun Watson has started every game.

keyMatchups.title: Ravens run game vs depleted interior
keyMatchups.body: The Browns' run defense is near the bottom of the league in EPA and worst in explosive runs allowed, and two of its interior tackles are out. Baltimore has run for 108 yards or more every week. This is the clearest edge on the board.

keyMatchups.title: Browns pass rush vs Ravens protection
keyMatchups.body: Cleveland sacks quarterbacks at the 5th-best rate, and Huntley went down four times at Atlanta. A backup center makes it worse. If Jackson sits, the Browns' best unit has a path to drive-killing sacks.

keyMatchups.title: Watson's sack problem vs a weak rush
keyMatchups.body: Cleveland allows the league's highest sack rate, but Baltimore generates pressure at only the 28th-best rate, and Hendrickson is out. Watson's bad line should still stall drives, especially since the Browns cannot run to stay out of obvious passing downs.

nextGame.watch: Whether Jackson is cleared. If he is, the passing game reverts to its top-five form and -4.5 looks short. If not, Henry's carry count against the Browns' depleted interior decides it.

restOfSeason.body:
The offense's efficiency is real but will cool against a tougher slate: Jacksonville's 3rd-ranked defense, Tampa Bay's 5th and the Chargers' 6th, plus two dates with Cincinnati. Expect scoring closer to 25-27 than 29. The defense's underneath soundness should hold. Its pass-rush and deep-coverage problems will bite against Buffalo's top offense and the better passing teams, so points allowed should stay in the low 20s. Penalties and special teams are the most likely areas for a new staff to improve.

The close-game record (0.75) and slight win surplus are modest enough that little regression is owed. With a healthy Jackson this is a 10-11 win team. The division is still open, with every rival at 3-2, and six divisional games make up the back half.
swingFactors: Jackson's ankle and how many games Huntley starts
Hendrickson's return to a 28th-ranked pass rush
Cleaning up line penalties under the new staff

bets.reason: Cleveland ranks 29th in rush EPA allowed and last in explosive runs, and it has two interior tackles out with its every-down linebacker questionable. Baltimore leaned harder on Henry with Huntley and ran for 208 yards at a top-10 defense.

The net EPA gap is wide (5th vs 23rd), and Cleveland's 3-2 rests on a -3.8 point differential and 1.26 wins over expectation. Baltimore already won by seven on the road with its backup. The number likely bakes in Jackson doubt, so a Jackson return is pure upside.

confidence.note: Five games, mostly against weak defenses, with Jackson's status and a new coaching staff adding uncertainty.
